chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Johnny Hodges and the Trumbauer influence on his alto sound
summary: He says both he and Hodges were influenced by Frank Trumbauer, and that a feeling for a sound is learned by emulating it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Can you comment on your kind of alliance in your sound with Johnny Hodges? People have always mentioned that.
Oh, yes, of course. But I think we were both influenced by Frank Trumbauer, pretty much.
Uh-huh, which you've mentioned, yeah. How did you develop that? Was it difficult to --
No, I don't think so. I think if you have a feeling for something, it's like a youngster in this day and age who -- if he hears an electronic sound, he'll try to we're living in
emulate it without electronics. And he'll try to do it on the instrument he's playing.
We don't hear people playing like Johnny Hodges anymore.
Oh, there are people, I suppose and I as a matter of fact, I hear people on occasion who have some indentation into their lifestyle and everything else, that comes out. So there's something of that.
